title: Manipal Health Sets Price Band for Nearly $1 Billion IPO, Opens July 29
excerpt: India's second-largest hospital chain operator targets $8 billion valuation after cutting its earlier range, with subscription opening next week.
body:
• Manipal Health Enterprises has set a price band of ₹560-590 per share for its ₹9,270 crore ($960 million) IPO, India's second-largest this year
  • The Temasek-backed hospital chain is targeting an $8 billion valuation, down from the $10-12 billion range initially marketed in April
  • Public subscription opens July 29 and closes July 31, with anchor investor bidding on July 28
  • Proceeds will primarily repay debt from its aggressive acquisition spree, including the ₹6,400 crore Sahyadri Hospitals purchase last year

Manipal Health Enterprises, operator of one of India's largest private hospital chains, has set the price band for its initial public offering at ₹560-590 per share, aiming to raise approximately ₹9,270 crore ($960 million) in what will be the country's second-largest listing this year.

The Bengaluru-based company and its existing shareholders will offer as many as 164.5 million shares when subscription opens on July 29, according to a newspaper advertisement published on Friday. Bidding will close on July 31, with anchor investors getting a one-day window on July 28.

Valuation Trimmed Amid Market Jitters

At the upper end of the price band, Manipal Health is targeting a valuation of roughly $8 billion — a marked retreat from the $10 billion to $12 billion range floated when it began meeting institutional investors in April. The recalibration reflects cautious sentiment toward large public offerings as tensions in the Middle East continue to rattle global markets, Bloomberg News reported last week.

https://x.com/ETMarkets/status/2080492056133390396

Even at the reduced valuation, Manipal's IPO will be the second-largest primary market offering in India this year, trailing only SBI Funds Management's $1.03 billion listing earlier in July. First-time share sales in India have raised $5.3 billion so far in 2026, compared with $7.1 billion through the same period last year, according to Bloomberg-compiled data.

Where the Money Goes

The offering comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹8,000 crore and an offer for sale of ₹1,210 crore by existing investors. Shareholders offloading stakes include Temasek Holdings' Imperius Healthcare Investments, TPG Capital's TPG SG Magazine, Manipal Education and Medical Group India, Seventy Second Investment Company, and others.

The bulk of the fresh capital is earmarked to repay borrowings at subsidiary Manipal Hospitals Pvt Ltd, with ₹5,378 crore set aside for debt reduction. Another ₹574 crore will be used to acquire the minority stake in step-down subsidiary Sahyadri Hospitals, with the remainder going toward general corporate purposes.

That debt largely stems from an aggressive acquisition strategy under founder Ranjan Pai. Manipal bought Columbia Asia's India operations for ₹2,100 crore in 2021, picked up controlling stakes in AMRI Hospitals for ₹2,300 crore in 2023 and Medica Synergie for up to ₹1,400 crore in 2024, then acquired Sahyadri Hospitals from the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan for roughly ₹6,400 crore in July 2025 — financed in part by a credit line from KKR's insurance business.

Scale and Competition

The result of that dealmaking is a network of 48 hospitals with 12,367 beds spread across 14 states and union territories, offering services ranging from outpatient care to tertiary and quaternary interventions in cardiology, oncology, transplants, and neurosciences. That puts Manipal squarely in competition with Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, Max Healthcare, and Fortis Healthcare — all publicly traded.

"There is enough appetite in the market for the pipeline of good companies that have lined up for FY27."

— Ramesh Srinivasan, MD & CEO, Kotak Investment Banking

Kotak Mahindra Capital, Axis Capital, and the Indian units of Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Jefferies, UBS, and DBS Bank are managing the offering.

What to Watch

The IPO's reception will be closely watched as a barometer for India's broader primary market recovery. Manipal Health filed its draft red herring prospectus with SEBI on March 25 and received the regulator's observations — effectively its approval — on July 3. The company had also considered a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹1,600 crore, which would reduce the fresh issue size if completed.

For diaspora investors tracking India's booming healthcare sector, Manipal's listing offers direct exposure to a hospital operator that has rapidly scaled through acquisitions and now faces the challenge of integrating those assets while servicing significant debt. How the market prices that balance sheet risk at ₹560-590 per share will set the tone for the second half of India's 2026 IPO season.
